citation: Iyengar N, Peng CK, Morin R, Goldberger AL, Lipsitz LA. Age-related alterations in the fractal scaling of cardiac interbeat interval dynamics. Am J Physiol 1996;271(4):R1078-R1084. Fantasia Database, PhysioNet (Goldberger et al. 2000).
record_used: subject f1y01 (young healthy adult), the first 5-minute RR window (391 RR intervals) -- the SAME git-tracked root the sibling Poincare and HRA cases use. The aging comparison uses all 10 subjects (5 young + 5 old).
pipeline: readRDS(rr5min_f1y01) -> PhysioECG::ecgHRVautonomic (NEWLY-AUTHORED op): the Toichi cardiac autonomic indices from the Poincare 4-SD bounding box -- CSI = L/T (sympathetic), CVI = log10(L*T) (vagal), CSI_Modified = L^2/T, where L = 4*SD2 and T = 4*SD1. The reference re-computes them with NeuroKit2 hrv_nonlinear (a bit-exact check; peaks reconstructed from the integer-ms RR at 250 Hz so NeuroKit2 sees the identical RR). Deterministic.
note: The tracked input is agent/eval/data/poincare-hrv/rr5min_f1y01.rds (the same 5-min f1y01 window the Poincare/HRA cases use). The Toichi (1997) cardiac autonomic indices are read off the Poincare plot's 4-SD bounding box: the long axis L = 4*SD2 and short axis T = 4*SD1, giving CSI = L/T (cardiac sympathetic index), CVI = log10(L*T) (cardiac vagal index), and CSI_Modified = L^2/T (Jeppesen 2014, used in seizure detection). ecgHRVautonomic is a NEW op authored to fill this gap (the ecosystem had the raw SD1/SD2 via ecgHRVpoincare but not the clinical CSI/CVI indices). It reproduces NeuroKit2's hrv_nonlinear CSI/CVI/CSI_Modified BIT-FOR-BIT (max |diff| 0): SD1 = SDSD/sqrt(2) (universal), SD2 = geometric paired-projection (the Toichi/NeuroKit2 convention, which differs by a small O(1/n) amount from ecgHRVpoincare's analytical closed-form SD2). The finding: the Cardiac Vagal Index is higher in the young (mean 4.90) than the old (4.55), robust across the cohort (5/5 young above the old mean) -- the parasympathetic decline of autonomic aging, complementing the DFA (alpha1 rises) and Poincare (SD1 falls) aging results on the same cohort.
